abstract: The Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) represents a large open science resource designed to enable detailed investigations of typical and atypical brain development across the perinatal period. It consists of 1228 multimodal magnetic resonance image examinations of the fetal and/or neonatal brain from 1173 participants, together with collateral demographic, clinical, family, neurocognitive and genomic data. All subjects were studied in utero and/or soon after birth with a single MRI scanner using specially developed scanning sequences with novel motion-tolerant imaging methods and optimised for the changing properties of the developing brain. The neonatal data has been described and released separately. The fetal data release consists of multimodal data from 273 subjects scanned between 20 + 6 and 38+2 weeks (+days) of gestation, with some fetuses imaged more than once to provide longitudinal data creating 297 datasets in total. The data include: high resolution and motion corrected T1 and T2 weighted anatomical images; high temporal resolution functional and multi-shell high angular resolution diffusion MRI; and multimodal age-resolved atlases; together with demographic, family and clinical data, genomic and epigenomic data and follow-up neurodevelopmental assessment at around 18 months. This paper describes the dHCP fetal image acquisition, reconstruction and processing protocols, summarizes the available data, and provides information on how it can be accessed.
